applies_why: The judge text decides whether witnesses on the cited-in line count as unanswered against the C3 link, which is exactly what K-G4 governs.
quote: WHY: no PRESSED line, no RETRACTED line, and no statement that names a pressing round and quotes it, for D2 vs C3; ... every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence... and names that round' — reading one: any use of a cited verse against a link requires the quoted pressing sentence and round; reading two: only counting a verse as an UNANSWERED witness requires that quote, while treating it as answered or retracting does not. I weighed the two and adopted the second.
why: The judge counted no verse as an unanswered witness (it explicitly found each one answered and retracted the ground), and it itself flagged the absence of any quoted-and-named pressing statement, so it did not treat any unpressed citation as counting.
